elements.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 12.4 now reads "Customer may develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory," removing the former "Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire ... for twenty-four months thereafter" prohibition; no other operative restriction on Customer's businesses, products, fields, or territories remains, and retained Section 12.3 confirms "Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete ... commitment."

elements.element: The restriction covers only a named competing product.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: after the edit there is no competing-product restriction binding Customer at all, so the narrowing requirement is vacuously satisfied by the stronger preferred outcome.

elements.element: The restriction applies during the term only.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the "During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter" temporal reach was deleted along with the prohibition; no post-term or in-term covenant on Customer survives.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the twenty-four-month tail was removed and no duration attaches to any Customer covenant, so no period can exceed 12 months.

elements.element: The restriction permits Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: rendered 12.4 affirmatively permits Customer to "develop ... any product or service that competes with Vendor," and 12.3 preserves Customer's freedom to develop any product or service.

Condition does not apply: rendered 12.4 affirmatively permits Customer to "acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory," and 12.3 preserves the right to acquire any product or service.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the operative prohibition on Customer developing, marketing, selling, or acquiring competing products (including the term-plus-24-month tail and the undefined "any product or service that competes with Vendor" scope) is gone, and nothing else in the cited language binds Customer's fields, products, or territories.

Minimality defect: the rule's redline guidance is to delete the restriction, but the drafter instead installed a new affirmative permission in 12.4 that merely restates rights already granted by retained Section 12.3 ("Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service ... in any field or territory"). This duplicates an existing operative term and adds a provision no checklist element requires. Repair by striking Section 12.4 in its entirety (or, if a placeholder is wanted, marking it "[Intentionally omitted]") rather than re-granting the same permission.

Intent is preserved: no defined term, cross-reference, or commercial mechanic is left dangling, and the edit removes rather than creates the prior contradiction with Section 12.3's no-non-compete acknowledgement.
Severity remains high: the original clause was a post-term, undefined-scope non-compete on Customer in walk-away territory, so the deviation classification is correct.
